$comment: Canonical response security-header values for my-web-2026 (Issue #449). This file is the single source of truth: src/http/security-headers.ts emits these values for every Worker-generated response, and scripts/check-security-headers.mjs asserts that public/_headers carries the same strings for Cloudflare Static Assets. Editing a value here without editing public/_headers (or the reverse) fails `pnpm run validate:fast`.

referrer_policy.$comment: `host` is the fallback for every Worker-generated response. `tool_app` is used for a Tool artifact served under the manifest's delivery.artifact_path (/tools/<slug>/app/...); a Tool bundle is third-party-shaped content and must not leak the host URL to whatever it fetches.

$denied_permissions_rationale: The list is deliberately explicit and minimal rather than a blanket deny-all. A feature that is NOT listed keeps the browser default allowlist ('self'), so a future Tool that needs a new capability does not have to amend the host baseline first. Each listed feature has no plausible use on this site: bluetooth/hid/serial/usb are hardware bridges, camera/display-capture/geolocation/microphone are capture devices, payment and xr-spatial-tracking are platform-gated products. microphone is listed because at least one registered Tool (mic-level) needs it — that is exactly why the grant is per-Tool (delivery.iframe.allow in src/tools/manifest.json) rather than host-wide.
